items.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: I would love to go back and spend a couple of years and listen, and that would be great to experience that, to meet some of these people... there’s definitely one concert, in 1963 there was a concert, in November, that the Dave Brubeck Quartet performed. And it was a legendary concert.

ctx.x: So he must have been like a catalyst for Brubeck’s writing in those kind of oddball time signatures because he was so good at it.

They heard him warming up, playing a five-four rudiment. And it caught the ear of Dave Brubeck. And he says well what is that? And he says well it’s a para diddle diddle with a para diddle, it comes out to five-four time. A basic drummer’s rudiment. And he asked Paul Desmond to write something. He says well why don’t we write something in five- four time, and thus, “Take Five.”
Umm. That was a fortuitous little encounter. Didn’t they do that thing in seven also? “Unsquare Dance.”
